question: On 2 February 1971, in the city of which country was the historic Ramsar Convention signed to conserve wetlands of international importance?
explanation:
The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands. It was signed on 2 February 1971 in the city of Ramsar, on Iran’s Caspian Sea coast, and entered into force in 1975. India joined the Convention on 1 February 1982. World Wetlands Day is observed every year on 2 February. (Sources: official Ramsar Secretariat portal; Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India.)

unit: Unit 5: Environment and Ecology; Uttarakhand Wetlands
question: Asan Conservation Reserve, declared Uttarakhand’s first Ramsar Site in October 2020, is located in which district?
options: Udham Singh Nagar, near Nanak Sagar
Haridwar, on the banks of the Ganga
Dehradun, at the confluence of the Asan and Yamuna rivers
explanation:
Asan Conservation Reserve, covering approximately 4.44 square kilometres, is the Asan Barrage wetland in the Vikasnagar/Dakpathar area of Dehradun district, where the Asan and Yamuna rivers meet. It received formal recognition on 21 July 2020 and was declared Uttarakhand’s first Ramsar Site—and India’s 38th Ramsar Site—in October 2020. It is an important winter habitat for migratory birds, including ruddy shelducks, pochards and mallards. (Sources: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India; Uttarakhand Forest Department.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Uttarakhand wetlands and biodiversity | Level: Easy | Question Type: Direct MCQ]

unit: Unit 5: Environment and Ecology; Uttarakhand National Parks
question: Which national park in Uttarkashi district, spread across the catchment areas of the Tons and Supin rivers, is associated with the central government’s Snow Leopard Project?
explanation:
Govind National Park was established in 1990; the wildlife sanctuary in the area dates to 1955. It covers about 472 square kilometres in the Rupin–Supin valleys of Uttarkashi district, within the Tons drainage system. Rare and threatened species found here include the snow leopard, brown bear, musk deer and monal. The source states that the Government of India launched Project Snow Leopard here. (Sources: Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun; Uttarakhand Forest Department.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Uttarakhand national parks and wildlife | Level: Moderate | Question Type: Direct MCQ]

unit: Unit 5: Environment and Ecology; Environmental Movements
question: On which date did Gaura Devi lead 27 women in Reni village to embrace trees and stop forest felling during the Chipko Movement?
explanation:
The Chipko Movement began in Gopeshwar in 1973 through the Dasholi Gram Swarajya Mandal led by Chandi Prasad Bhatt; a major turning point came on 26 March 1974 in Reni village in Chamoli district’s Niti Valley. When forest-department and contractor workers arrived to cut trees, 27 village women led by Gaura Devi embraced the trees and challenged them. The source further states that, following the recommendation of the Virendra Kumar Committee, the Uttar Pradesh government imposed a ten-year ban on felling across 1,200 square kilometres of forest. (Source: Anupam Mishra, history of the Chipko Movement; Uttarakhand environmental history.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Uttarakhand environmental movements—Chipko | Level: Easy | Question Type: Direct MCQ]

unit: Unit 5: Environment and Ecology; Van Panchayats
question: Under the rules of which year was the community institution known as the Van Panchayat, a system of local self-management of forests, formally established by the British government?
explanation:
Following the recommendations of the Kumaon Grievances Committee (1921), the British colonial administration introduced the Kumaon Forest Panchayat Rules, 1931, recognising traditional forest rights of mountain communities. The rules gave village forest panchayats local, community-based authority to protect forests, manage fuelwood and fodder, and support regeneration. The source states that more than 12,000 Van Panchayats currently function in Uttarakhand and that 50% reservation is provided for women. (Sources: Uttarakhand Forest Panchayat Rules; Professor Shekhar Pathak’s work on colonial Kumaon forest history.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Uttarakhand’s Van Panchayat system | Level: Hard | Question Type: Direct MCQ]

unit: Unit 4: Science and Technology; Major Scientific Institutions
question: The 3.6-metre optical telescope at Devasthal in Nainital district, established through cooperation between India and Belgium, operates under which major scientific research institute?
options: Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES)
explanation:
The Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES) is an autonomous astrophysics institute under the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, based at Manora Peak in Nainital. ARIES established the 3.6-metre Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT) at Devasthal, about 50 kilometres from Nainital at an altitude of approximately 2,450 metres. The source describes it as Asia’s largest steerable optical telescope and states that it was jointly inaugurated by the prime ministers of India and Belgium in 2016. (Sources: official ARIES Nainital portal; Department of Science and Technology.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Major scientific institutions in Uttarakhand | Level: Moderate | Question Type: Direct MCQ]

unit: Unit 4: Science and Technology; Space Missions
question: What is the main technical feature of NISAR, the Earth-observation satellite developed jointly by ISRO and NASA and launched in 2025, according to the source?
options: It is a space observatory devoted only to studying solar flares and the Sun’s corona.
It is described as the first satellite with dual-frequency L-band and S-band radar, mapping the entire Earth in 3D every 12 days.
It searches for water molecules at the Moon’s south pole.
It is an autonomous sonar satellite dedicated to mineral exploration on the ocean floor.
explanation:
NISAR (NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint space mission of NASA and ISRO. The source says it was launched in 2025 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, using a GSLV rocket. It describes NISAR as the first satellite to use dual-frequency synthetic-aperture radar: an L-band system built by NASA and an S-band system built by ISRO. The source says the mission can map global changes in Earth’s surface every 12 days, including glacier melt, landslides and earthquake-related deformation, even through clouds and darkness. (Sources cited in the source text: ISRO mission update 2025; NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory NISAR report.)

unit: Unit 4: Science and Technology; Human Spaceflight
question: Which Indian astronaut was selected by ISRO as the prime Indian crew member for the India–US Axiom-4 mission to the International Space Station in 2025?
explanation:
For Axiom Space’s commercial Ax-4 mission, operated in cooperation with ISRO and NASA, Indian Air Force Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla was selected as the prime astronaut, while Group Captain Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair was named as the backup. The source states that, 41 years after Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma’s 1984 spaceflight, Shukla became the second Indian to travel to space and the first Indian astronaut to visit the International Space Station. (Sources cited in the source text: official ISRO press release; NASA’s Axiom-4 announcement.)

unit: Unit 4: Science and Technology; ISRO Missions
question: What was the primary objective of ISRO’s SpaDeX mission, conducted in 2025 as a technological step towards the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) and a lunar sample-return mission?
options: To destroy old inactive satellites by bringing them into Earth’s atmosphere
To install a coronagraph at the Sun–Earth L1 point
To test laser communication in deep space
To demonstrate autonomous rendezvous and precision docking of two satellites—the chaser and the target—in space
explanation:
SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment) is an important ISRO technology-demonstration mission. The source says it was launched in 2025 by a PSLV rocket. Two separate satellites—the Chaser and the Target—were placed in low Earth orbit and brought together to demonstrate India’s ability to perform rendezvous and automatically dock them using an indigenous robotic system. The source describes this technology as essential for the proposed Bharatiya Antariksh Station, targeted for 2035. (Sources cited in the source text: ISRO technology bulletin 2025; Press Information Bureau.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: No | Topic: Current affairs—indigenous ISRO technology, 2025 | Level: Moderate | Question Type: Direct MCQ]

question:

| A. John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton | 1. Physics: artificial neural networks and machine learning |
| B. David Baker, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper | 2. Chemistry: computational protein design and AlphaFold |
| C. Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun | 3. Medicine: discovery of microRNA and gene regulation |
| D. Nihon Hidankyo | 4. Peace: the Hibakusha movement for nuclear disarmament |

Codes: A B C D
explanation:
The 2024 Nobel Prize matches are: Physics—John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton, for foundational discoveries and inventions enabling machine learning with artificial neural networks; Chemistry—David Baker for computational protein design, and Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for protein-structure prediction using AlphaFold2; Medicine—Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun for the discovery of microRNA; Peace—the Japanese organisation Nihon Hidankyo, representing survivors of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings, for its work towards a world free of nuclear weapons. Therefore, the code is 1–2–3–4. (Source: official Nobel Foundation announcements, nobelprize.org.)

question: Which statement about the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, held in February–March 2025, is true?
options: The tournament was played only in Lahore and Karachi, Pakistan.

question:
Consider the following statements about the fiscal targets announced in India’s Union Budget 2025–26:

1. The fiscal-deficit target for financial year 2025–26 was set at 4.4% of GDP.
2. Under fiscal consolidation, the government aimed to fulfil its earlier roadmap of bringing the fiscal deficit below 4.5% by 2025–26.

Which of the statements above is/are correct?
explanation:
According to the source, both statements are true. In the Union Budget 2025–26 presented by the Union Finance Minister, the fiscal-deficit target was set at 4.4% of gross domestic product (GDP), down from the revised estimate of 4.8% for 2024–25. The government also sought to meet the post-pandemic fiscal-consolidation roadmap, which had committed to bringing the deficit below 4.5% by FY 2025–26. Capital expenditure was kept above ₹11 lakh crore. (Sources: key features of the Union Budget 2025–26; Ministry of Finance, Government of India.)

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Constitutional and Electoral Reforms
question: Who chaired the High-Level Committee on ‘One Nation, One Election’, whose report was approved by the Union Cabinet?
options: Ram Nath Kovind, former President of India
explanation:
The eight-member High-Level Committee chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind submitted its report on simultaneous elections to the President; the Union Cabinet approved it. The source says the committee recommended a two-phase approach: first, hold elections to the Lok Sabha and all State Legislative Assemblies together; then, within 100 days, conduct elections to municipalities and panchayats. unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Indian Languages and Culture
question: After the Union Cabinet granted ‘Classical Language’ status to five additional languages, what is the total number of officially recognised Classical Languages in India?
explanation:
In October 2024, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi granted Classical Language status to five additional languages: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali. Before this decision, six languages had the status—Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013) and Odia (2014). The total therefore rose to 11. (Source cited in the source text: official notification of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.)
